x: Bowers gained a double, winning the 100 yards and 220 yards, with Frank Simmons 4th. The 440 yards was an easy win for Frank Webb, with Tommy Morrell, taking up sprinting, 2nd.
Webb and Morrell were 3rd and 5th respectively; 440 yards and 880 yards, Marchant and Carnie, 1st and 4th; the mile, Cohen, Carter and F.

Thomas, together with Tommy Morrell, represented us in the Mile, and they both ran well against a much stronger opponent. Tom Carter, without any "real" opposition, ran a training 3 miles and reeled off his laps in faultless style.

With Len Herbert 6th and Tom Morrell 8th we scored an easy win in the team championship, an honour which we have secured in 1925, 1926, 1929, 1930, 1931, 1933, 1934, 1935, 1936 and 1937.

Dick Tobin lead the field out at a fair pace, then bunched together were Carter, Bill Lucas, Clinton, Abberton, Eales, Blowfield, Penny, with Footer and Morrell a little behind, and Len Herbert at the rear.
The food and drinks were catered for by the ladies of the Club, Mesdames: Carter, Shepherd, Savage, Penny and Morrell, while their better halves thoroughly enjoyed themselves entertaining the "kids".
Stimpson, Carter, LES BENNETT, Shields, Penny, Morrell, Shaw, Beaumont, and ARTHUR ALLUM pose with their awards at a pre-war White City meeting.
